one_liner: Read-only, zero-copy Rust XML DOM parser; 2-3.5x faster than libxml2, no mutation or writing.
what_it_does: roxmltree parses an XML document into an immutable, iterator-based DOM tree for read-only queries (e.g. find element by id, walk descendants). It does not support tree mutation or serialization back to XML. Parsing behavior intentionally mimics Python's lxml rather than being fully XML-spec-complete. The API is idiomatic Rust (Document::parse, Node iterators), not a drop-in replacement for libxml2's C API or bindings.
how_it_is_fast: Node/attribute names, text, comments, and processing instructions are kept as Range<usize> slices into the original input buffer instead of being allocated and copied, so the tree is largely zero-copy. The tree itself is a flat, vector-backed arena (a modified version of the ego-tree crate) rather than a pointer-chasing linked structure. Scanning uses the memchr crate for fast byte search, and the crate forbids unsafe code and supports no_std, avoiding both libxml2's own allocator/type-conversion layer and the FFI marshalling overhead the benchmark's rust-libxml bindings add on the libxml2 side.
when_to_use: Read-only extraction/querying from well-formed, UTF-8 XML (config files, SVG, feeds, data interchange)
Latency- or throughput-sensitive parsing of small-to-large (not multi-GB) documents where libxml2 FFI overhead matters
Pure-Rust builds that must avoid a C dependency or unsafe code (no_std-compatible via memchr)
Workloads needing exact source position tracking per node/attribute for diagnostics (positions feature)
One-shot parse-then-read pipelines where no later edit/round-trip-serialize step is needed
when_not_to_use: Any workflow that mutates the tree or writes XML back out — not supported at all
Documents needing DTD resolution/validation — DTD support is not complete
Non-UTF-8 input — not supported (libxml2 handles this)
Very large documents where memory is tight: peak RAM runs ~6-8x file size (author's own 1.1GB file measurement: 7.6GB peak)
HTML or non-well-formed markup — no HTML mode, unlike libxml2

integration.dependencies: memchr (sole dependency; the README's own alternatives table lists roxmltree as having 0 dependencies, which conflicts with Cargo.toml)
integration.platforms: any (pure Rust, no_std-compatible, no arch-specific requirements documented)
integration.thread_safety: not documented explicitly; the parsed tree is read-only/immutable after Document::parse
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial — same read-only DOM-query idea as libxml2 but a different, iterator-based Rust API, and it drops mutation, writing, DTD, and HTML support

gotchas: Disabling the `positions` feature saves 8 bytes/node and part of the attribute overhead but removes original-document position tracking

README's benchmark tables are internally inconsistent: huge_roxmltree is 2,997,887 ns/iter in the libxml2 comparison table but 3,147,424 ns/iter in the streaming-parser table, where huge_quick_xml instead shows exactly 2,997,887 ns/iter — looks like a copy-paste slip in one of the two tables
Project states any panic is a critical bug to report, i.e. panics are not expected/allowed even on malformed input
libxml2 in this benchmark is driven through the `rust-libxml` FFI wrapper crate, not called natively, so its measured time includes binding overhead
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick roxmltree over pugixml or lexbor/libxml2 when you need a pure-Rust, no-unsafe, no-C-dependency parser for read-only XML querying and don't need mutation, writing, DTD, or HTML support; pick pugixml or lexbor instead when you need in-place tree editing, serialization, or HTML parsing.
verified_claims_summary: On an Apple M1 Pro, using `cargo bench` with the bencher/libtest harness, roxmltree parsed four synthetic XML sizes 2.2-2.3x faster than libxml2 (called via the rust-libxml FFI crate) for medium/large/huge files and ~3.5x faster for tiny files; no rustc version, compiler flags, or libxml2 version are stated.
status_note: Actively maintained (last commit 2026-09-22, 537 stars) and dual MIT/Apache-2.0 licensed, small pure-Rust crate that's easy to vendor or pin.
